title: My grandma's land appropriation
description: My grandmother farmland became gradually smaller in rural China as local development plans changed the landscape around her. From 1996 until 2017, I followed how the land she once farmed was incrementally taken for infrastructure and urban expansion. Eventually, she was relocated and the place where her home and fields once stood is now occupied by a gas station and a major road.

In Western media, land appropriation in China is often portrayed as sudden and conflict-driven. While such conflicts do happen, many cases unfold more gradually and with little conflict or confrontation. By focusing on the personal story of my grandmother, this piece shows the broader transformation of China’s rural landscape. This is a dynamic rendition of the original story.

title: data driven op-ed illustrations
description: Selected work for Dutch newspaper NRC, where I create a biweekly data-driven illustration column. I pitch story ideas, conduct independent research, and translate the findings into illustrations for the op-ed section, published both in print and online.
Click here to view them all in Dutch.

title: Who wins the Nobel Prize?
description: I designed a collection of visualisations showing that the overwhelming majority of Nobel Prize laureates are wealthy, Western men. While representation is slowly improving, the disparity remains significant. The project combines more complex data visualisations with simpler charts, where I could loosen the strict, clean style and incorporate illustrations directly into the graphics. I wanted to add playfulness while keeping the data readable and engaging.
Click here to view the project at NRC.

title: editorial illustration
description: Selected editorial illustration work from the past 12 years, where I explore visual metaphors to capture the essence of each story. Illustrations have been created for various newspapers and magazines, including Trouw, NRC, De Volkskrant, and VPRO.

title: Dutch general elections 2021
description: Part of a series of analysis videos leading up to the 2023 Dutch national elections, each focusing on a key political issue.

For this episode on the housing crisis, I translated data research into visuals. Colleague journalists analysed parliamentary motions and how each party voted, and I turned their findings into a heatmap, both as a physical set pieces and animated overlays, to highlight key insights. By combining tangible visuals with motion design, I helped make complex political data clear and engaging for viewers.

title: Doris the Diver, Martime Museum Amsterdam
description: Doris the Diver is an adventurous, maritime museum experience for families with children aged 2 years and older in the National Maritime Museum (Het Scheepvaartmuseum) in Amsterdam.

Children aged 2+ and their company: from friends to parent, carer, aunt, grandfather or babysitter – can get acquainted with the National Maritime Museum, love for water and the maritime world in a playful way.
Together, visitors can explore the worlds under and on the surface of the water and follow Diver Doris on her quest from sea to land.
Doris the Diver is a permanent exhibition and opened in October 2022.

title: Modern slavery
description: his story reports on modern slavery in Ecuador, Lebanon, Thailand and the Netherlands. Given an audio testimony and some location footage as reference, I developed the storyboard and decided what to reconstruct frame by frame. Because hand-drawn animation is time-intensive, I worked with reporters to shorten the testimonies to what was feasible without losing the story. The editor opted for illustrations over staged video reconstruction to signal clearly it was a retelling. I chose a frame-by-frame approach to combine my illustration style with animation. Working within Nieuwsuur's visual style, I sourced additional reference material to draw from.

title: Climate change past, present and future
description: This video explains the complexity of climate change by looking into the past, present and future.

I translated the script visually into a metaphor of a rubik’s cube to depict this complicity: changing one factor affects the others. I designed both the physical cubes in the set and the motion graphics that animate the story, creating a visual language that makes the interconnections tangible and understandable.

title: Demonstrations in Iran
description: In late 2025, widespread protests erupted in Iran over rising oil prices and growing dissatisfaction, only to be violently suppressed while the government cut off internet access, leaving video and information scarce.

This project started with a dataset of verified protest videos, each tagged by incident type and location. My role was to translate that data into a series of maps and a timeline. I used tags to plot separate maps showing different types of incidents, and selecting which videos to surface to show that demonstrations were spreading across the country rather than concentrated in one place.
